text: Left ribbon lists the active pods and clusters, each with an indicator: waiting or working, how many agent pods run, and a circular 0-100% context gauge.
Main view is a chat with smart message loading showing agent activity: past inputs, outputs, thinking and tool calls.
The web UI theme matches the ros2-lerobot-sverve-platform web UI.
Pods and groups of pods (clusters) can be defined with their config and discarded.
A headless API orchestrates and communicates with the sessions and is the unified router for future use at scale (tatara, magic-trainer).
Messages to a cluster go round-robin: the agent that has been free the longest receives the message.
Agents in a cluster can communicate with each other.
A cluster's agents share a PVC on RWX rook-ceph CephFS.

Every new session starts with any-mcp preinstalled: no derived agent image; a per-cluster rendered onStart hook pip-installs any-mcp from the pinned git tag into a venv and writes its config before the wrapper starts any session.
The setup lets the user test whether round-robin plus multiple agents plus inter-agent messaging speeds up thinking and execution and improves robustness and correctness.
Decentralised microservices coordinating only through a Postgres queue (CNPG), with the orchestrator calling the Kubernetes API itself.
Integration with claude-code-wrapper is verified against the real wrapper, not only a fake.

Delivered as a new component code/agent-orchestrator with public GitHub origin szymonrychu/agent-orchestrator, CI, the orchestrator image pushed to Harbor (no derived agent image), least-privilege RBAC and a kind end-to-end test that installs the repo's Helm chart.

In-cluster callers cannot reach the API: it enforces a direct-peer source allowlist (ORCH_ALLOWED_CIDRS, health routes exempt), and ClusterSpec is hardened (image allowlist ORCH_AGENT_IMAGES, reserved env keys rejected, claude.passthrough_env rendered, any_mcp_config validated against the any-mcp schema, caps on replicas, PVC size and cluster count).

A failed send never wedges round-robin and is retried automatically: the reservation is released on every non-accept outcome, definite non-accepts (unavailable, gone) are retried with bounded attempts and exponential backoff while busy is requeued at once and config error or rejected fail at once, the wrapper client maps every HTTP status, and one clock (Postgres now()) is used for all comparisons.
Two dispatchers never double-dispatch under READ COMMITTED: the claim writes agents.last_dispatched_at and the pick reads it, proven by a forced-interleaving test.
Singleton failover is fast and loud: libpq keepalives and tcp_user_timeout on the lock connection, a lock-held heartbeat, exit non-zero on loss, tested with a blackholed holder.

A slow or ambiguous send is never sent twice: a send timeout well below the dispatching stale cutoff, a heartbeat on the dispatching row, and an ambiguous outcome (or a stale dispatching row) is checked against the wrapper (did a turn carrying this message id start, via snapshot current_turn_id and the turn records' metadata) before any automatic retry; started means sent, a definite not-started after the settle window is retried with backoff, and no answer by the deadline fails it as ambiguous with Retry as the user's choice.

Everything lives in namespace agents and clusters are told apart by labels (no ORCH_CLUSTERS_NAMESPACE): object names use the reserved agent-<slug> prefix with the slugs orchestrator and orchestrator-* rejected, and the reconciler refuses to apply over or prune any object lacking both the managed-by and cluster labels.
The reconciler cannot read Secrets: secrets verbs are create, patch and delete only, in namespace agents; cluster Secrets are deleted by deterministic name and never listed.

Session adoption is correct: adopt only creating, ready or busy sessions, resume stopped or failed sessions that have a transcript, otherwise create a new one, and a 404 on submit triggers re-bootstrap.
Sessions and check Jobs use one rendered workdir path (/workdir/<spec.workdir>), pinned by a test in each of the renderer, session bootstrap and check jobs tasks.
A targeted message never blocks the queue: the claim skips a message whose target is busy and fails one whose target is gone with reason target_gone.
Dispatch is FIFO per cluster under concurrent dispatchers, enforced by a per-cluster transaction-level advisory lock in the claim.

Discard deletes everything: the cluster's Kubernetes objects, its PVC and its whole chat history (messages, events, turns, commands, checks). An optional pre-discard hook (a command or webhook URL from settings, or a webhook URL from the cluster spec; none by default) receives the cluster's full history export as JSONL before anything is deleted, and a failed hook blocks the deletion.
AskUserQuestion is disabled in the rendered wrapper config; agents get an appended system prompt instructing them to ask questions in writing as a numbered list, each with a recommended answer.

agent-orchestrator ships its own Helm chart chart/agent-orchestrator, started from helm create: the four component Deployments with the migrate initContainer, Service, ServiceAccount, the reconciler Role and RoleBinding, the settings ConfigMap and Secret refs; a Postgres connection is required by default (URL, host/user/password or existingSecret), CNPG is optional (cnpg.enabled false by default), ingress is optional with annotations from values and no homelab defaults; helm lint and helm template unit tests run in CI, which publishes the chart to oci://harbor.szymonrichert.pl/charts with immutable versions.
